primaryQuery: Folding Carton Closures: Tuck End, Lock Bottom or Auto Bottom?
customerDecision: Choose a folding carton closure around the filled product, the packing method and the way the customer opens it. Tuck ends, manually locked bottoms and pre-glued auto bottoms solve different assembly problems. None has a universal load capacity. Compare physical samples using the same product and board specification, then approve the closure, insert and artwork together before production.

primaryQuery: Corrugated Mailer or Shipping Carton: What to Specify
customerDecision: A corrugated mailer or shipping carton must be specified as part of a complete packed system. Start with the product, its inner protection, packed weight and distribution route. Then agree the box style, board construction, closure and verification plan. A style code identifies the design; it does not prove that a particular board or packed configuration will survive transport.

primaryQuery: Custom Paper Bags: Size, Handles and Loaded Sample Checks
customerDecision: Size a custom paper bag around the finished contents in their carrying orientation, including tissue and accessories. Specify width, side gusset and height with a drawing. Choose handles and reinforcement around the loaded weight and intended use, then evaluate an assembled, loaded sample. Paper weight and a premium handle finish do not establish a safe carrying capacity by themselves.

primaryQuery: Packaging Reorders: Control Specifications and Version Changes
customerDecision: A packaging reorder should reference an approved specification and sample, not just an old purchase order or photograph. Confirm that the product, material, artwork, insert, packing method and delivery route are unchanged. Record every proposed substitution or revision before production. When a change affects fit, appearance or transport performance, agree the sample or test evidence needed to approve the revised configuration.
